finding.claim: UpyunCallbackAuth writes a 401 on signature-verification failure but does not abort or return, so c.Next() still runs ProcessCallback and completes the upload session.
finding.source: Unauthenticated POST /api/v4/callback/upyun/:sessionID/:key with attacker-controlled body and headers (routers/router.go:491-496).
finding.sink: controllers.ProcessCallback -> callback.ProcessCallback(c), which completes the upload session (protected state change).

trace.note: On error, c.JSON(401, ...) written; no c.Abort() and no return
ProcessCallback executes and completes the upload

finding.guards_checked: upyun.ValidateCallback (not in repo, outcome only observed via err branch). Compared with QiniuCallbackValidate (callback.go:47-52) and OSSCallbackValidate (callback.go:73-76), which both abort on failure; only the Upyun branch falls through. UseUploadSession not in repo. Precondition: attacker must know sessionID and key from callback URL, which are issued to the uploader.

finding.claim: Direct-link create (PUT) and delete (DELETE) under file/source are gated only by files:read scope, not files:write.
finding.source: Any token holding only files.read scope.
finding.sink: controllers.GetSource (PUT source, creates public direct links) and controllers.DeleteDirectLink (DELETE source/:id) - state-changing operations.

trace.note: source := file.Group("source") inherits only read scope
source.PUT("") GetSource registered with no RequiredScopes(FilesWrite)
source.DELETE(":id") DeleteDirectLink registered with no RequiredScopes(FilesWrite)

finding.guards_checked: Group-level FilesRead scope; ValidateBatchFileCount on PUT (router.go:775); HashID(SourceLinkID) on DELETE (router.go:779). No write-scope check on either route. Ownership checks inside service/explorer not in repo.

finding.claim: COS, S3, KS3, OBS and OneDrive upload callbacks rely solely on UseUploadSession; no signature/auth middleware is applied.
finding.source: Unauthenticated GET/POST callback requests with sessionID and key in path.
finding.guards_checked: UseUploadSession (not in repo). Contrast OSS (OSSCallbackAuth), Upyun (UpyunCallbackAuth), Qiniu (QiniuCallbackValidate), Remote (RemoteCallbackAuth). Security depends on whether :key is a high-entropy per-session secret compared by the middleware - unverified.

finding.claim: PATCH user/reset/:id has no signature or captcha middleware; authorization rests entirely on the token in the body inside the service.
finding.source: Unauthenticated PATCH request with attacker-controlled JSON body (UserResetService) and id param.
finding.guards_checked: HashID decoding only. No SignRequired, no CaptchaRequired (contrast router.go:391-397 for the request step). Token validation inside service/user not in repo.

finding.claim: 2FA OTP verification endpoint has no visible route-level rate limit or captcha, enabling brute force of the 6-digit code.
finding.source: Attacker holding a twoFaSession token plus guessed OTP codes.
finding.sink: service/user Verify2FA, which issues a full auth token on success (UserIssueToken).

trace.note: token.POST("2fa") registered with no captcha or throttle middleware

finding.guards_checked: Route-level: none visible. Attempt limiting inside service/user Verify2FA not in repo.

finding.claim: Share passwords are accepted as URL path segments (s/:id/:password), which tends to leak into access logs and Referer headers.
finding.source: Share link URL containing password path segment.
finding.sink: Request logging and Referer propagation of the password (information exposure).

trace.note: ShareRedirect handles request and redirects via service.RedirectTo

finding.guards_checked: Logging middleware and Referrer-Policy not in repo; not checked.

finding.claim: POST admin/settings returns settings gated only by admin:read scope; if secret-valued settings are included, a read-scoped token can exfiltrate them.
finding.source: Token with admin:read scope (or admin user) posting to admin/settings.

trace.note: settings.POST("") has no additional write scope

finding.guards_checked: IsAdmin and AdminRead at group level. Whether returned settings contain secrets is in service/admin, not in repo.

finding.claim: BatchDeleteShare writes an error response and then, without returning, writes a success response, producing two JSON bodies.
finding.source: Authenticated request to share DELETE with a service error.
finding.sink: HTTP response body (logic defect; not an authorization bypass).

trace.note: c.JSON(200, success) written unconditionally, no return

finding.guards_checked: None relevant; this is a response-handling defect.

finding.claim: GET setting/2fa is gated only by user:info:read; if Init2FA persists a pending secret, a read-scoped token can mutate account 2FA state.
finding.source: Token with user info read scope.
finding.sink: user.Init2FA (possible persistence of a pending 2FA secret).

trace.note: setting.GET("2fa") registered with no write scope

finding.guards_checked: Group-level UserInfoRead scope and LoginRequired. Whether Init2FA writes to the DB is in service/user, not in repo.
